brief: SPX melted into the weekend, retesting 7k, led by AI/Semis selling, then worsened by late-day NVDA SEC-probe and Iran-strike-risk headlines, after capital-markets activity failed to stabilize risk appetite. GS flags that high-touch flow was not commensurate with the move: elevated top-down/ETF trading (39% of tape) and thin top-of-book liquidity ($4mm, near YTD low) amplified price action. Long-only semis sellers found buyers frozen; Nasdaq VIX hit its highest since Covid, though panic remains anecdotal. HF and LOs finished the week moderate net sellers. S&P logged a 7th straight red session (rarest since Feb 2020, 1 of 5 in 25 years), down ~8.6% on the week, the worst since Covid and first comparable week since the Iran War (Apr 4). CTAs are now net short $19bn (26th %ile) after selling $57bn in a month, and models forecast continued selling next week toward 7596/7540/7119 triggers; implied move into Thanksgiving week is 3.27%. Prime data shows HFs net sold for a 3rd straight week via heavy single-stock shorting (largest since Jun '22) and rising ETF shorts (largest since March); 9 of 11 sectors were net sold.
